routes.approach: Dispatch this dependency-ready proof. The exact reviewed type elaborated in the shared slot with import Proofs.EilenbergWatts and open scoped ModuleCat.Algebra. Use Classical.choose_spec for the precise EilenbergWatts witness named by the statement and unpack its pure-tensor universality and map law. For the forward implication, check the scaled identity on each pure tensor using the map law, balancing, scalar agreement on B, and the left-scalar rule. Use the uniqueness clause with the common balanced function to identify the two linear maps. For the reverse implication, test a scaled identity on the lifted regular module at pure b (ULift.up 1). Centrality identifies left multiplication by algebraMap Complex R z with right multiplication on the regular module. Balancing then gives equality of the pure tensors for the two actions on b. Construct a retraction of b ↦ pure b (ULift.up 1) by extending the balanced function (b,x) ↦ b·x.down to B, using commuting actions and the order of multiplication in the opposite ring. Apply that retraction. Split these checks into a scalar identity lemma, a regular retraction lemma, and a full-subcategory lemma. Lift EqualScalars.ι ⋙ ew.functor with the forward implication. For essential surjectivity, take ew.inverse of a complex-linear object and use the underlying natural iso from ew.counitIso, in the direction giving Complex-linearity of its image. The reverse implication puts the chosen preimage in EqualScalars. Lift the counit to the full subcategory and use asEquivalence on the lifted forward functor. The final field is equality of the composed functors. Prove it from the defined lift, checking objects and maps if reduction does not suffice.
